html:
The Swan River Colony was the British settlement founded in 1829 on the Swan River in southwest Australia, with its capital at Perth and its port at Fremantle. In 1832 it took the name Western Australia.

It was led by Captain James Stirling, and unlike New South Wales it began as a colony of free settlers, with no convicts. Settlers got land in proportion to the money, goods and servants they brought. Many found the soil sandy and poor, workers were scarce, and the colony grew slowly. Short of labour, it began taking convicts in 1850.

The land was the country of the Noongar peoples, among them the Whadjuk around Perth, the Ballardong of the Avon valley, and the Bibbulman, Wiilman and Wadandi further south. Settlers took their waterholes and hunting grounds, and the Noongar resisted. The Whadjuk leader Yagan was killed in 1833, and in 1834 Stirling led an attack on the Pinjarup people at Pinjarra in which many were killed.
